BPC-RSDF 30-trial confirms that global baseline-teacher KL can make the method worse than RSDF and even baseline on seed7.
RSDF gain remains below target: +4 on seed7 and +2 on seed13 under matched 30-trial confirm30, averaging +3 points rather than the required +5.
SPRC shows full-parameter L2 protection alone does not prevent harmful correction
extreme tail tasks 5 and 7 remain zero across both seeds
additional LT simulation dataset still pending
CGRBC seed7 gain collapses on seed13; rare weighting active_count is too sparse
RLCT improves seed13 over CGRBC but loses seed7; freezing non-LLM capacity is too restrictive
next method must preserve action-space behavior directly, not only parameter-space distance
NB-TCAD shows positive/negative expert-state margins are mostly already satisfied, so offline TCAD cannot localize rollout relation failures
next experiments must test rollout-state eligibility or closed-loop diagnostics before another correction loss
Tail-Focal BC confirms that offline action-token sharpening can redistribute capacity across tasks and does not reliably solve closed-loop tail failures
Fixed-init action gain falsifies simple execution-side action scaling: seed7 unchanged and seed13 only +1 point.
Small Spatial-LT screens must use fixed init ids when judging diagnostics, because unfixed 10-trial variation produced misleading swings.
BC-gradient projection via two backward passes is incompatible with the current FSDP full-shard training path; do not pursue PCGrad here without a non-FSDP or custom FSDP-safe implementation.

AHP-RSDF is checkpoint-level fusion rather than end-to-end training; if it works, the paper framing must justify it as parameter-space behavior preservation or convert it into an equivalent training constraint.
AHP-RSDF fails cross-seed reliability: seed7 +6 fixed-init but seed13 -1; action-token head drift is not the main damage channel.
C-RSDF confirms that more conservative checkpoint fusion is not the fix: seed7 only +2 over fixed-init baseline and below RSDF/AHP, seed13 ties fixed-init baseline while task0 and task6 remain weak.
The next method must be based on closed-loop rollout-state error diagnosis/correction, not another parameter-fusion microvariant.

CGRBC.conclusion: confusion gating gives seed7 signal but is not stable

CGRBC_pulse5.conclusion: short pulse is conservative but does not lift

NB-TCAD.conclusion: detaching the positive branch makes TCAD too inactive; offline expert-state margin is not the Spatial-LT bottleneck

Tail-Focal_BC.conclusion: training-time focal action CE is active but unstable; it sharpens offline tail tokens without solving rollout-state shift

Tail_Action_Gain_unfixed.conclusion: mixed and confounded by uncontrolled init-state/randomness; requires fixed-init replication before causal interpretation

Tail_Action_Gain_fixedinit.conclusion: fixed init ids remove the apparent swings; simple tail-only action scaling is not causal or sufficient

AHP_RSDF.conclusion: protecting llm embed/lm_head during RSDF fusion is not sufficient; damage is distributed across relation/action layers

C_RSDF.conclusion: cross-seed sign-consensus BARC delta is too blunt; rejected and used as evidence to pivot away from fusion microvariants

CRGR.conclusion: behavior-risk weighted replay alone is not stable; it needs baseline behavior preservation or stricter acceptance gating

BPC_RSDF_GPU_TEACHER_OOM.conclusion: loading the frozen baseline teacher on GPU replicated under two-rank FSDP caused 47GB-per-GPU OOM; CPU teacher fallback is required for this stack

BPC_RSDF_confirm30.conclusion: 30-trial confirmation rejects BPC-RSDF; baseline-teacher KL over-preserves baseline behavior and suppresses RSDF correction

GPRC.conclusion: Rejected as final despite seed7 gain: direct positive last-action contrast damages seed13 task3/task6 relation behavior; do not launch 30-trial confirm.

rollout_diag_pair.conclusion: RSDF creates real closed-loop gains by shortening successful rollouts on relation-sensitive tasks, but it also trades away tasks 2/7/8 depending on seed. Damage is tied to relation-specific gripper timing, rollout length, and action norm shifts rather than a global action-scale issue.
